FINDING_ID: IM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.83  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: The shim’s own boundary declaration misframes responsibility for the immune subsystem by excluding `_failure_handler.py`, even though the analytical boundary and the shim’s imports include `FailureHandler` and `CorrelatedFailureModel`. This is not merely a doc typo; it distorts cross-subsystem review scope by making failure detection appear outside the immune layer while `process_round()` immune integration necessarily consumes recovery actions/failure records from that component. Evidence: the docstring says `The immune layer review boundary is: _types.py + _immune.py + _manager.py.` while the import section has a dedicated `# ── Immune layer ──` block importing `FailureHandler` and `CorrelatedFailureModel` from `_failure_handler.py`. Existing prior findings already cover the omission itself; the missed part is the ownership error: the document assigns immune sensing to `_immune.py` only, but remediation depends on `_failure_handler.py` contracts, so the boundary statement breaks cross-cutting analysis.  
PROPOSED_FIX:  
<<<<
The immune layer review boundary is: _types.py + _immune.py + _manager.py.
====
The immune layer review boundary is: _types.py + _immune.py + _failure_handler.py + _manager.py.
Failure detection (`FailureHandler`) is part of the immune subsystem because its
outputs drive diagnosis, remediation, and round-level immune control flow.
>>>>
VERIFIED: TRUE

FOLLOW: This change requires updating any review instructions, decomposition manifests, and module inventories that currently route failure detection outside immune review. It also means interface summaries must include `FailureRecord`/`CorrelatedFailureModel` contracts if they are used to drive diagnosis or remediation. Definitive stance: the boundary ownership is wrong and must explicitly include `_failure_handler.py`.

FINDING_ID: IM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.80  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: The public compatibility surface is structurally inconsistent with the stated immune API because the shim documents `_manager.py` as owning `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS`, `apply_diagnosis`, `_apply_transform`, and `process_round`, but exposes only `DynamicManager`. Prior findings cover missing exports individually; the missed cross-cutting issue is that this prevents external tooling from inspecting or testing immune policy as data/entrypoints after refactor, forcing callers to go through the whole orchestrator object instead of the documented policy surface. Evidence: the docstring names those symbols in `_manager.py`; the import line is only `from bench.dm._manager import DynamicManager`.  
PROPOSED_FIX:  
<<<<
from bench.dm._manager import DynamicManager  # noqa: F401
====
from bench.dm._manager import (  # noqa: F401
    DynamicManager,
    _REMEDIATION_CHAINS,
    apply_diagnosis,
    _apply_transform,
    process_round,
)
>>>>
VERIFIED: TRUE

FOLLOW: If these names are actually instance methods rather than module-level functions, this fix will fail import-time and reveals a deeper documentation/API mismatch: the docstring must then be corrected to stop advertising them as importable shim symbols. Either way, the current state is inconsistent. Any `__all__` added later must include or intentionally exclude these names in alignment with the chosen public contract. Definitive stance: the manager-side immune API is mis-exported and must be made consistent one way or the other.
